description: The graph illustrates the loss ratio (%) of various models as a function of TFLOPs (trillion floating-point operations), with the x-axis representing computational cost on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1e7 to 9e8, and the y-axis showing the loss ratio from 94% to 100%. The legend identifies five distinct models: Vanilla (purple, dashed line with square markers), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line with triangle markers), SepLLM (n=128) (blue, solid line with diamond markers), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid line with circle markers), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid line with circle markers). The Vanilla model maintains a nearly constant loss ratio of approximately 100% across all TFLOPs. SepLLM (n=64) shows a rapid increase in loss ratio from around 97.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs to a peak of about 100% at 4e8 TFLOPs, followed by a slight decline. SepLLM (n=128) starts at approximately 97.2% and steadily increases to around 99.8% at 9e8 TFLOPs. SepLLM (n=64, H) begins at about 97.5% and rises to approximately 100% at 4e8 TFLOPs, then slightly decreases. SepLLM (n=64, H/T) exhibits a sharp increase from 94% at 1e7 TFLOPs to a peak of about 99.5% at 3e8 TFLOPs, followed by a gradual decline to approximately 98.8% at 9e8 TFLOPs.
